skill.name: npm-helper
skill.description: NPM and Node.js package management guidance for project setup, dependency management, auditing, workspaces, and publishing workflows.
skill.summary: Guide Node.js projects through package setup, dependency maintenance, npm audits, workspace workflows, and publishing tasks.
skill.author: CuriousLearner

security_audit.summary: Most static backtick, URL, dotenv, .env, .npmrc, and Yarn config findings are false positives from Markdown examples or benign package configuration. Confirmed risks are the sudo chown guidance and persistent shell profile changes in the EACCES section. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.issue: Privileged ownership repair commands are recommended for npm permission errors.
remediation.suggestion: Remove sudo chown examples for global modules. Prefer nvm, a user-level npm prefix, or documented manual recovery with explicit confirmation.

remediation.issue: The skill appends a PATH change directly to ~/.bashrc.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users what to add manually, detect the active shell, and require approval before modifying shell startup files.

remediation.issue: Troubleshooting guidance deletes package-lock.json during reinstall steps.
remediation.suggestion: Back up lock files first and explain that deletion can change dependency resolution before suggesting cleanup commands.

remediation.issue: Publishing commands can affect authenticated npm registry state.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation for login, version changes, publish, registry, access level, and tag before execution.

static_findings.snippet: - Use exact versions in production (`npm install --save-exact`)
- Use `npm ci` in CI/CD for faster, reliable installs
- Use `npx` instead of global installs when possible

semantic_findings.title: Destructive Dependency Cleanup Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The troubleshooting section advises removing node_modules and package-lock.json before reinstalling. Removing the lock file can change dependency resolution and should require backup and user approval.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The commands are present in the troubleshooting workflow and can materially change project dependency state. Legitimate repair is possible, so this is medium confidence rather than malicious intent.

semantic_findings.title: Registry Publishing Workflow Requires Confirmation
semantic_findings.description: The publishing workflow includes npm login and npm publish commands. If an agent executes them without explicit confirmation, it could use credentials or change public registry state.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow is a legitimate package-maintainer task, but the commands affect authenticated registry state. The risk depends on whether the agent asks for confirmation.

content.value_statement: Node.js projects often need consistent package setup, updates, audits, and troubleshooting. This skill gives practical npm, Yarn, and pnpm guidance for common workflows.
actual_capabilities: Compare npm, Yarn, and pnpm commands for installation, updates, scripts, and audits.
Guide new project setup with package.json fields, scripts, dependencies, and .gitignore entries.
Explain dependency versions, lock files, peer dependencies, and workspace configuration.
Provide troubleshooting steps for module resolution, cache problems, permission errors, and slow installs.
Outline package publishing preparation, dry runs, versioning, tags, and registry settings.
limitations: It provides command guidance, but users must approve filesystem, registry, and shell changes.
It does not verify package safety beyond the audit commands shown in the skill.
Examples may need adaptation for Windows, CI systems, and company package registries.
It cannot resolve private registry credentials without user-supplied context.

use_cases.title: Set Up a New Node.js Project
use_cases.description: Create package metadata, install dependencies, add scripts, and choose a package manager for a new service.

use_cases.title: Maintain Dependencies Safely
use_cases.description: Review outdated packages, understand version ranges, run audits, and plan controlled updates across a team codebase.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Package Release
use_cases.description: Check package metadata, run validation commands, inspect publish contents, and choose npm publishing options.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me initialize a Node.js project with npm. Include dependencies, dev dependencies, scripts, and files I should create.

prompt_templates.title: Fix an Install Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this npm install error and suggest safe steps before deleting files or clearing caches: [paste error].

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Update Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my package manager setup and propose an update plan that keeps lock files stable and avoids breaking changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Monorepo Release
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a package release workflow for this workspace. Include validation, versioning, dry-run publishing, and registry safety checks.

output_examples.input: I need to create a small Express project with TypeScript.
output: A recommended npm setup with runtime and development dependencies.
Script suggestions for development, build, test, lint, and type checks.
Notes on files to create and what should be ignored by version control.

output_examples.input: npm install fails after a package upgrade.
output: A diagnosis path that checks installed versions, lock file state, peer dependency warnings, and cache health.
Safer cleanup guidance before removing generated folders or lock files.
A short list of commands to run only after user confirmation.

output_examples.input: I want to publish a scoped package.
output: Release checklist for metadata, build outputs, tests, and package contents.
Guidance to use dry-run publishing before changing the registry.
Notes about access level, tags, and confirming the account before publish.

best_practices: Review command effects before allowing changes outside the current project.
Keep lock files committed and use clean installs in CI.
Run audits and tests after dependency updates or package manager migration.
anti_patterns: Do not run sudo npm commands as a routine fix for install issues.
Do not delete lock files without understanding dependency resolution changes.
Do not publish packages before confirming account, registry, contents, and tag.

faq.question: Can this skill work with npm, Yarn, and pnpm?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains equivalent commands and notes where package manager behavior differs.

faq.question: Does it install packages automatically?
faq.answer: It can suggest commands. Users should approve installs and any filesystem changes before execution.

faq.question: Can it help with npm audit results?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains audit commands, update options, and safer ways to review vulnerability fixes.

faq.question: Is it safe for private registries?
faq.answer: It can describe registry configuration, but users must provide policy details and protect tokens.

faq.question: Can it configure monorepos?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers npm, Yarn, and pnpm workspace examples for common repository layouts.

faq.question: What should I review before publishing?
faq.answer: Confirm package contents, version, registry, account, access level, and tags. Use a dry run first.
